note: Glossary of terms and abbreviations used on screen. Definitions only: no limits, factors or model numbers. Sources are ids from references.json.

terms.definition: Formed mostly from nitrogen in the air at high flame temperature. Regulations report NOx as NO₂ on a dry, reference-O₂ basis.
NO formed from air nitrogen and oxygen in hot burned gas. The rate rises steeply with temperature, so peak temperature matters more than average temperature.
Product of incomplete combustion. Rises when the flame is too cold or too short to finish oxidation, for example at low load in lean premix combustors.
Main product of burning carbon in the fuel. Specific CO₂ follows fuel use, so it falls when efficiency rises.
CO₂ plus other greenhouse gases weighted by their global warming potential. Here it adds unburned methane (methane slip) to the CO₂ from combustion.
Warming effect of a gas relative to the same mass of CO₂ over a stated time horizon.
Share of the fuel gas that leaves the engine or turbine without burning. It is not part of plain CO₂ but counts in CO₂e.
Fuel or partly burned fuel in the exhaust. In gas engines it is mostly methane (see methane slip).
Soot and other particles, typical of diesel combustion in the fuel-rich spray core. Shown qualitatively in this app; not computed.
Formed from sulfur in the fuel (diesel sulfur or H₂S in fuel gas). Computed by mass balance from the fuel analysis.
Analysers installed on the stack that measure concentrations and O₂ continuously. Site data from CEMS takes priority over model values.
Gas-turbine combustor that premixes fuel and air lean to keep flame temperature low, without water or steam injection.
Fuel and air mixed before the flame with excess air. Low flame temperature gives low NOx, but the flame nears its stability limit and CO rises when it gets too cold.
Adjustable vanes at the compressor inlet. Closing them reduces airflow at part load so a single-shaft turbine can hold its flame temperature.
Compressor, turbine and load on one shaft at constant speed. At part load it closes the IGV first; once the IGV runs out, flame temperature falls and CO shows a cliff.
Gas generator and free power turbine on separate shafts. Gas-generator speed falls with load, so the operating window shifts and narrows instead of showing a cliff.
Load range in which model NOx and CO both stay at or below the selected limits. Indicative; depends on the limits entered.
Actual air divided by the air needed for complete combustion. Above one means lean (excess air). It is the inverse of φ.
Actual fuel-air ratio divided by the stoichiometric ratio. Below one means lean. In the diesel model φ also stands for engine load.
Mass of air per mass of fuel. The stoichiometric AFR is the value for complete combustion with no excess oxygen.
Heat released by burning the fuel with water leaving as vapour. Efficiencies in this app are on an LHV basis.
Piston at its highest point. Crank angle is counted from TDC of the combustion stroke.
Crank-angle direction for timing. Retarding the timing moves combustion later (towards ATDC): lower NOx, lower efficiency.
Crank angle at which combustion starts (fuel injection in the diesel, spark in the gas engine). A main NOx lever in engines.
Part of the exhaust returned to the intake to dilute the charge and lower peak temperature. Not available in this model.
Shaft power divided by fuel energy (LHV), after friction losses.
Fuel mass per unit of shaft energy. Lower BSFC means higher efficiency and lower specific CO₂.
Highest pressure in the cylinder during the cycle. Earlier timing and higher boost raise it.
S-shaped curve for the fraction of fuel burned versus crank angle, used for heat release in the cylinder model.
Gas-turbine cycle: compression, heat addition at near-constant pressure, expansion. Efficiency rises with pressure ratio and turbine inlet temperature.
Air-standard engine cycles with heat added at constant volume (Otto), constant pressure (Diesel) or both (dual). They set the ideal ceiling for real engines.
Outlet pressure divided by inlet pressure of a compressor (or the whole turbine cycle).
Similarity rules for turbomachines: flow scales with speed, head with speed squared, power with speed cubed.
Temperature of the burned gas with no heat loss. Highest near stoichiometric mixtures; the main driver of thermal NOx.

terms.expansion: Parts per million by volume, dry
terms.definition: Concentration in dry exhaust. Always quoted with its reference O₂ so values from different units can be compared.
Mass concentration at a stated reference temperature, pressure, O₂ and dry basis. The regulation basis is shown next to every value.
Converts a measured concentration to a fixed O₂ level so that dilution with excess air does not hide emissions.
Label on emission numbers from correlations. The trend is physical; the absolute level is calibrated to typical literature values, not to site or vendor data.
Measured values entered for a real unit (for example from CEMS or a stack test). Shown with priority over model values and marked as site data.
Limit typed by the user from an operating permit or a manufacturer guarantee, used where the regulation table has no limit (for example turbine CO).
